title: Examination Results Queries
description: Draft public-service guidance; review questions must be resolved before publication.
clarifying_questions: Does the issue concern a missing or incorrect mark, subject, absentee entry, pending result or cancellation?
Which examination and release year does it concern?
Are you applying through the relevant institution or education office?

claims.text: The historical manual identifies absentee appeals, missing marks and reinstatement queries.
The public query page directs examination queries through heads of institutions and Sub-County Directors of Education.

citations.locator: Period Of launching queries after release of Results

claims.text: The public query page defines missing or incorrectly captured marks or grades, missing subjects or papers, registration-related pending results, suspected-irregularity pending results and appeals against cancelled results as distinct query categories.

The 2018 QMIS guide documents selecting the relevant query type, completing the displayed fields, attaching the documents requested by the Required List, submitting, checking success feedback and tracking progress through Status.
The 2026 charter says examination-result queries should be raised within 30 working days after release and routes examination-related queries through KNEC agents and online submission.

The charter lists late-query penalties by examination family: KES 5,000 for KCSE, post-school and teacher examinations, and KES 3,000 for KCPE, KPSEA/KILEA and KJSEA/KPLEA. These amounts require exact examination, year, query type and triggering event before use.

The captured public query page uses 30 calendar days and says appeal documents must reach KNEC through institutional or education-office channels, while the 2026 charter uses working days. The conflict must remain blocked until the controlling rule is confirmed.

unresolved_questions: Confirm the current evidence checklist and authorized route for each results-query category.
Resolve calendar-day versus working-day wording and establish the applicable triggering event.
Confirm how appeals involving suspected irregularities or cancelled results differ from correction queries.
